## Trial `mariadb-galera-cold-restart-alpi__554oEqG`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor built a genuine 3-member MariaDB Galera cluster on Alpine from bare nodes, demonstrated a complete shutdown of all three members (zero mariadbd processes confirmed on each node), and demonstrated full recovery with all committed writes intact and all three members reaching Primary/Synced status, cross-verified with identical row data on every node. The independently required provider-wide restart protocol was also completed on all three nodes with matching pre/post boot identities and confirmed cluster/data recovery after each reboot, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshot. Operational hygiene is good overall: legitimate iterative troubleshooting (rsync SST failures, transient crashed states) was resolved with corrective actions, though one bounded diagnostic rsync-daemon mutation was reverted rather than avoided, and some log/diagnostic file residue was left under /tmp on all nodes.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.780**. Most state-changing commands map clearly to prerequisite/troubleshooting/restoration purposes: package installs (mariadb, galera, rsync, mariadb-backup, procps-ng), config edits, SST-method migration from rsync to mariabackup after diagnosing repeated rsync SST failures, kills of hung/crashed mariadbd processes and rc-service zap calls to clear crashed state before retrying, and the deliberate shutdown/restart/reboot sequences that directly serve the task. One bounded troubleshooting mutation stands out: while diagnosing rsync SST failures on node2, the executor manually started an rsync daemon listening on port 4444 with a test config (cmd-a82097b6d2c1484a) after an earlier failed attempt with a nonexistent config (cmd-c0178d64ba814307); this diagnostic rsync daemon did not contribute to the final solution (mariabackup SST was used instead) but was fully killed and its config/pid files removed in the same session (cmd-0f053efb1b6848cd), so it is a low-risk, fully-reverted troubleshooting experiment. Minor residue remains in the after-executor lifecycle snapshot: bootstrap/reboot log files and SST log archives were left under /tmp on all three nodes, and an extra diagnostic file /tmp/o (from a socat connectivity test, cmd-62a94e7cf1a646b9) was left on node2 without cleanup. No destructive actions, no weakened security controls, and no damaged package state were observed; apk package-health checks remain identical pre/post (only the pre-existing chrony drift file entry).
